title: Normalized etale exceptional comparison preserves projection mates
statement: Fix the finite coefficient datum of [sk-def-purity-conv], with $A=A_{E,n}$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the constructible exceptional inverse images of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:S\to T$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and a tensor-invertible $N\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ [pur9-cs-def-invertible] with a chosen inverse $N'$ and evaluation $N\otimes^LN'\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$, let $$\kappa_{h,K,N}:Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N\longrightarrow Rh^!(K\otimes^LN)$$ be the morphism corresponding, under the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(Rh_!P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(P,Rh^!Q)$ of $Rh_!\dashv Rh^!$ used in [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], to the composite $$Rh_!(Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N)\cong\bigl(Rh_!(Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N)\otimes^LN'\bigr)\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{h,Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N,N'}\otimes1}Rh_!(Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N\otimes^LLh^*N')\otimes^LN\cong Rh_!Rh^!K\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{h,K}\otimes1}K\otimes^LN,$$ where $\operatorname{PF}$ is the specified projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection], $\varepsilon_h$ is the counit, and the unlabelled isomorphisms are the evaluation, the tensor associators and unit constraints, and $Lh^*N\otimes^LLh^*N'\cong Lh^*(N\otimes^LN')\cong A_S$ through the tensor-pullback comparison $\mu_h$ of [def-exchange-projection]. (It does not depend on the choice of $(N',\text{evaluation})$; it is the conjugate of $\operatorname{PF}_{h,(-),N'}$ under $Rh_!\dashv Rh^!$ and $(-)\otimes^LN'\dashv(-)\otimes^LN$, and when $h$ is a closed immersion its inverse is the co-projection isomorphism of [lem-pur-coprojection].) Now let $e:U\to X$ be an etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $\rho_e:Re^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*$ be the normalized natural comparison of [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization], and let $\mu_{e;M,N}:Le^*(M\otimes^LN)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*M\otimes^LLe^*N$ be the tensor-pullback comparison of [def-exchange-projection]. Then for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and tensor-invertible $N\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$: $$\rho_{e,K\otimes^LN}\circ\kappa_{e,K,N}=\mu_{e;K,N}^{-1}\circ(\rho_{e,K}\otimes1):Re^!K\otimes^LLe^*N\longrightarrow Le^*(K\otimes^LN).$$ In particular $\kappa_{e,K,N}$ is invertible, and with $\operatorname{coProj}_{e,K,N}:=\kappa_{e,K,N}^{-1}$ one has $\mu_{e;K,N}\circ\rho_{e,K\otimes^LN}=(\rho_{e,K}\otimes1)\circ\operatorname{coProj}_{e,K,N}$.

source.place: Step 4(ii), etale-local comparison paragraph: rho intertwines the co-projection mate with the monoidality of Le*

proof.text: Write $F_h=Rh_!$, $G_h=Rh^!$, $P_h=Lh^*$ and suppress canonical tensor associators. All adjunctions used below are the constructible/etale-origin adjunctions, not ambient pro-etale adjunctions. The preservation assertion in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) put $G_hK$, $P_hN$, $G_hK\otimes P_hN$ and $K\otimes N$ in $D^b_{ctf}$. The same definition says the schemes are Noetherian in this finite-type field-base setting. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), choose bounded constructible etale origins for these inputs and for $K,N$. Their finite Tor amplitudes are reflected by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii). The comparison is fully faithful on these bounded-below objects by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Thus [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies to the specified projection map at $(G_hK,N)$, on both sites, and makes it invertible.

source.place: Step 4(ii): domain checks for the normalized etale/co-projection comparisons

proof.text:
Let $A=G_hK$, and denote by $T:F_h(A\otimes P_hN)\to F_hA\otimes N$ the three arrows preceding $\varepsilon_{h,K}\otimes1$ in the definition of $\kappa$. By [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws](3), under the evaluation $N\otimes N'\simeq A_T$ and its pullback,
$$\operatorname{PF}_{h,A\otimes P_hN,N'}\circ(\operatorname{PF}_{h,A,N}\otimes1_{N'})=1_{F_hA}.$$
Here the unit identifications are inserted: projection with the coefficient unit is the identity, since its proper factor is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and its open factor in [def-exchange-projection] is the unit constraint. Tensor this displayed equality with $N$ and insert the unit of $(-)\otimes N'\dashv(-)\otimes N$, the tensor-adjunction normalization specified in the statement. Its triangle identity contracts the inserted inverse twist. The resulting equality is exactly $T\operatorname{PF}_{h,A,N}=1$. Step 1 makes the projection invertible, so $T=\operatorname{PF}_{h,A,N}^{-1}$. Consequently the defining transpose is
$$q_{h,K,N}=(\varepsilon_{h,K}\otimes1_N)\operatorname{PF}_{h,G_hK,N}^{-1}.$$
This expression contains neither $N'$ nor its evaluation; injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the claimed independence of inverse data.

source.place: Step 4(ii): cancellation of the inverse twist in the explicitly specified projection mate

proof.text:
For completeness, the description as a conjugate and the closed-immersion normalization use the same arrows, not an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism. For a bounded constructible finite-Tor test object $P\in D^b_{ctf}(S,A)$, the invertible data [pur9-cs-def-invertible], the adjunction of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], and the projection map give the natural Hom chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,G_hK\otimes P_hN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes P_hN',G_hK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_h(P\otimes P_hN'),K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_hP\otimes N',K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_hP,K\otimes N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,G_h(K\otimes N)).$$
The projection arrow in this chain acts by precomposition with $\operatorname{PF}_{h,P,N'}$. Apply the chain to $P=G_hK\otimes P_hN$ and its identity. Expanding the two tensor adjunctions inserts $N'\otimes N$ and its evaluation and gives precisely the defining transpose of $\kappa$. This is the stated conjugate. When $h=i$ is closed, [lem-pur-coprojection] specifies coProj as the right-adjoint comparison induced by that same projection isomorphism with the inverse twist. Its Hom chain is the displayed chain in reverse, so its inverse is exactly $\kappa_i$.

source.place: Hom calculation and final Yoneda paragraph; identifies the normalization used in Step 4(ii)

proof.text:
We now prove the equality for etale $e$. It suffices to compute on the ordinary etale origins of Step 1. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify $P_e$, tensor and evaluation through $
u^*$. The exact equality in [lem-pur-projection-comparison-etale-origin] identifies the specified compactification projection maps. The exceptional functor and its adjunction are the transported ones of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] characterizes $ho_e$ by preservation of the transported sum/evaluation counit. The composite comparison $
u_U^*e^{-1}\cong e^{-1}
u_X^*$ is monoidal for these tensor comparisons, and the unit comparisons agree, by the composition and 2-isomorphism clauses of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Substitute these identifications in $q$ from Step 2 and in the two claimed maps. They become the corresponding etale maps. Full faithfulness from Step 1 then transfers the equality back; naturality handles arbitrary choices of origin isomorphisms.

source.place: Step 4(ii): specified projection and counit comparisons through the finite-level etale realization

proof.text:
On the etale sites write $F=Re_!$, $G=e^\times$, $P=e^*$, $S=D(e_{\Sigma!})$, $\epsilon:SP\to1$ for the fold counit, and $d:F\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ for the proper-support/sum comparison. These are available for the separated finite-type etale map between Noetherian schemes by [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact] and [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Put $p_{M,N}:SM\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}S(M\otimes PN)$ for the derived sum projection. By [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2),
$$d_{M\otimes PN}\operatorname{PF}_{e,M,N}=p_{M,N}(d_M\otimes1).$$
By the counit-preserving characterization of $\rho$ in [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization],
$$\epsilon_K S(\rho_K)d_{GK}=\varepsilon_K.$$
In particular these formulas identify the actual maps used in the item, including their counits.

source.place: Step 4(ii): normalized etale exceptional comparison via proper-support sum extension

proof.text:
Let $r_{M,N}=p_{M,N}^{-1}$. The fold-counit compatibility of [lem-asd-etale-sum-extension-tensor], applied with $(B,C)=(N,K)$ and moving $N$ to the right by the canonical symmetries, is the equality
$$\epsilon_{K\otimes N}S(\mu_{K,N}^{-1})=(\epsilon_K\otimes1_N)r_{PK,N}:S(PK\otimes PN)\longrightarrow K\otimes N.$$
The comparison called $P_{B,M}$ there becomes $r_{M,N}$ under these symmetries: the sum projection in [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2) sends $(s,m)\otimes n$ to $(s,m\otimes s^*n)$ on each lift, and the reverse termwise sum comparison sends that same tensor back. The cited fold-counit identity is an equality on unbounded derived categories, so this step does not infer equality of derived morphisms merely from stalk calculations. All tensor symmetries are the canonical signed symmetries, on both sides of that identity; the tensor-pullback comparison commutes with them because $e^*$ is symmetric strong monoidal [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons].

source.place: Step 4(ii): right-tensor form of the sum/evaluation counit identity

proof.text:
Put $B=GK\otimes PN$ and $Q=\mu_{K,N}^{-1}(\rho_K\otimes1):B\to P(K\otimes N)$. Its transpose under the normalized $F\dashv P$ adjunction is $\epsilon_{K\otimes N}S(Q)d_B$. By Step 6 and naturality of $r$ in its first variable this equals
$$\begin{aligned}
(\epsilon_K\otimes1)r_{PK,N}S(\rho_K\otimes1)d_B
&=(\epsilon_K S(\rho_K)\otimes1)r_{GK,N}d_B\\
&=(\epsilon_K S(\rho_K)d_{GK}\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{e,GK,N}^{-1}\\
&=(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{e,GK,N}^{-1}=q_{e,K,N}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is exactly the inverted projection-comparison equality of Step 5; the third is its counit-normalization equality [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility, lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization]. The map $\rho_{K\otimes N}\kappa_{e,K,N}$ has this same transpose, since $\kappa$ has transpose $q$ by Step 2 and $\rho$ preserves the counit. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] gives $\rho_{K\otimes N}\kappa_{e,K,N}=Q$. Step 4 returns precisely the asserted pro-etale identity.

source.place: Step 4(ii): explicit equality of the two projection-mate transposes

proof.text: The proved equality gives $\kappa_{e,K,N}=\rho_{e,K\otimes N}^{-1}\mu_{e;K,N}^{-1}(\rho_{e,K}\otimes1)$. Each factor is invertible, hence so is $\kappa_e$. Define $\operatorname{coProj}_e=\kappa_e^{-1}$; multiplying the proved equality on the left by $\mu_e$ and on the right by $\kappa_e^{-1}$ yields $\mu_e\rho_{e,K\otimes N}=(\rho_{e,K}\otimes1)\operatorname{coProj}_e$, with exactly the domains in the statement.
